sections.overview: The Great Pondhawk is a large green skimmer found across the Americas, from the southern United States south into South America.
sections.identification: The adult is mostly green with dark bands across the abdomen, a combination that helps distinguish it from other pondhawks.
sections.habitat: It is associated with ponds and other still waters; a Florida university account notes it in many parts of the state and in numbers during migration in south Florida.
sections.diet: Like other dragonflies, adults are aerial predators; the reviewed species sources do not provide a full prey list specific to this pondhawk.
sections.behavior: In an Amazonian campina study, this species was observed flying over open patches rather than concentrating in shaded parts of the sampled foraging habitat.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted identify its aquatic habitat but do not report species-specific courtship or egg-laying observations.
sections.ecology: Its open-area flight was linked in the Amazon study to behavioral and thermoregulatory differences among dragonflies, rather than to a demonstrated exclusive habitat requirement.
sections.conservation: A 2007 IUCN assessment is reported as Least Concern in the species records consulted; the date matters because it is not a recent population survey.
